name: KEYBOARD — ANSI TENKEYLESS
source: ANSI 87-key tenkeyless. 19.05mm key pitch and 18.0mm keycap tops are the industry standard (0.750in / 0.709in); 8mm bezel and 20mm case height are typical of a plate-mount TKL.

datum.note: front-left-bottom corner of the case, sitting on the desk top. Placed so the board centres roughly under the monitor and clears the sketchpad at x<600 and the mouse at x>1274.

envelope.note: FULL ASSEMBLY, not the case. Height runs from the underside of the feet (-8) to the keycap tops (+30); depth includes the 24mm cable stub behind the case. The case alone is 368 x 20 x 130 and is dimensioned on the `shell` part.

tilt.note: rear raised by the flip-out feet; the case itself is prismatic, which is how a real board works

parts.note: A WELL, NOT A SLAB. 8mm bezel all round, floor 8mm up so the caps sit in a 12mm recess. A slab has a flat top face, hidden-line removal draws nothing there, and the caps float.
parts.hiddenNote: The shell is the one part worth dashing: its far rim and well floor running behind the caps is what tells you the caps sit IN something. The caps themselves are deliberately not dashed — 87 sets of hidden edges is mush, not a drawing.

cap.note: 22mm tall so the cap top lands 30mm above the desk — 10mm proud of the 20mm rim

parts.rowNote: Widths in units. Negative entries are gaps and are what produce the function-row breaks, the offset navigation block and the arrow cluster's inverted T. Each row sums to 15u for the main block; the nav block sits 0.5u right of it.

features.note: flip-out feet, 8mm lift over 130mm depth — the 6deg tilt in `tilt`
num / caps / scroll indicators, let into the rear rim
USB-C exits the rear right of the case

dimensions.note: the one dimension that explains the whole part

leader.note: front-right top corner: outside the key field, on the side the sheet has room

keepout.note: never run a leader across the key field — it is the part being described
the front rim carries the width dimension; keep leaders off it

colourNote: A keyboard stays monochrome even in shot. Its own colour says nothing, and shot 4 spends its colour on the monitor and the workpapers.
